name: Sandefjord Airport, Torp
before:
Branded as an Oslo airport and 110 km away from it, which is the single most important thing to tell a client before they book. Torp sits 7 km north east of Sandefjord, and while it works as the low cost gateway for eastern Norway and the capital, the transfer to central Oslo is a long one.

For Vestfold itself it is simply the local airport, and a good one. The runway is 2,989 metres and airBaltic, Ryanair, Wizz Air, SAS and Norwegian all run scheduled services, with Wideroe keeping a base here for domestic and short international flying.

Since Rygge closed in 2016 it has been the second largest airport in eastern Norway.

Its origins are military. It was built largely with NATO funding in the 1950s as a base the United States Air Force could use in wartime, opened in July 1956 and took its first civilian flights in 1958.
after:
Ryanair sells it as Oslo Torp, but it is well over 100 km from Oslo, which is the single most important thing to tell a client before they book. Torp sits 7 km north east of Sandefjord, and while it works as the low cost airport for eastern Norway and the capital, the transfer to central Oslo is a long one.

For Vestfold itself it is simply the local airport, and a good one. Widerøe, Ryanair, Wizz Air, SAS, airBaltic and Norwegian all fly from here.

Since Rygge closed in 2016 it has been the second largest airport in eastern Norway.

Its origins are military. It was built largely with NATO funding in the 1950s as a base the United States Air Force could use in wartime, opened in July 1956 and took its first civilian flights in 1958.
